newsitem.title: USA: Sears to open 110 stores in New York state.
newsitem.headline: Sears to open 110 stores in New York state.

text.p: Sears, Roebuck & Co., citing improved economic conditions in New York state, said Friday it plans to open 10 full-line department stores and more than 100 freestanding, speciality stores across the state of New York during the next four years.

The stores, which include a full-line department store opening this fall in the New York City borough of Brooklyn, are expected to generate more than 5,000 new jobs and an additional $300 million in tax revenue, said Arthur Martinez, Sears Chairman.

"Due to improved economic conditions in New York State and (New York) City, we are aggressively looking for new sites to better serve the needs of residents who want convenient shopping in their own neighbourhoods," Martinez said in remarks prepared for delivery to a news conference in New York.

The nation's second largest retailer said this month it will begin a $20 million renovation of the former Alexander's department store in Brooklyn. When completed, the store will be the largest Sears in the metropolitan New York area and the second full-line store in Brooklyn.
Sears also is working on increasing its presence in other parts of New York City, including Manhattan, it said.
"We would like to add 10 full line department stores to the boroughs and the state by the end of the year 2000," Martinez said.

The company is involved in a bid to build a store on the New York Coliseum site at Columbus Circle near Manhattan's Central Park. The proposed store would be the first full-line Sears in Manhattan in the company's 110-year history, Sears said.
